report.trigger: The third-party payment gateway had a burst of HTTP 503 errors ('Service Unavailable (upstream capacity)') on POST /v1/charges. It ran from about 09:19:37Z to about 09:21:35Z on 2026-09-24.
report.root_cause: Deploy dep-8841 (commit a3f9c2e, checkout/payment_client.py, finished 09:14:47Z) changed the gateway retry policy in three ways: it added 503 to status_forcelist, set allowed_methods=None so non-idempotent POST charges are now retried, and set backoff_factor=0. With total=3, each failing checkout now makes up to 4 charge attempts back to back and runs for about 30-40 s. checkout-api holds its DB connection for the whole gateway call, including retries, so these long checkouts filled the 15-connection pool per instance (db_pool_in_use stayed at 15/15 from about 09:19:50 to 09:21:00). Every other request on checkout-api-3 then waited the full 10 s pool_timeout and failed with a 503. The retry change is the defect. Holding the connection across the gateway call is the existing design choice that let the retries use up the pool.
report.failure_mode: Customers got generic HTTP 503s on every endpoint, not just checkout. In the deployed replay, 124 of 5,576 requests failed. 105 were app-generated db_pool_checkout_timeout errors after a 10 s wait: 42 on GET /orders/{id}, 26 on GET /cart and 37 on POST /checkout. Only 19 were real gateway 503s passed through. Checkout p95 latency rose to about 40 s and read-request p95 to 10 s. checkout_5xx_rate peaked at about 70%.
contributing_factors: By design, checkout-api holds a DB connection through the whole payment gateway call, including retries (runbook 'Connection handling contract'). This ties pool occupancy to how long the gateway call takes.
The pool is small: 15 connections per instance (pool_size=5, max_overflow=10), and one pool is shared by read endpoints and checkout.
pool_timeout=10 s makes read requests queue for 10 s before failing, which pushed read p95 to 10,000 ms.
backoff_factor=0 means retries fire immediately and hit the gateway again while it is still failing.
allowed_methods=None retries non-idempotent POST charges, which risks double charges. This is a correctness risk as well as a load issue.
ruled_out: Gateway outage alone as the full explanation: with the old retry policy restored and the same burst, the replay showed 0 pool timeouts, 0 read-request 503s and 0 s of pool saturation. Only 93 checkout POSTs failed, as passed-through gateway 503s.
CPU or resource saturation on checkout-api-3: the dashboard showed cpu_percent at about 30-37% throughout.
A pool that is simply too small for normal traffic: with no gateway burst, the replay showed 0 errors and checkout p95 of 226 ms.

Raising pool capacity as the fix: at 30 connections, read 503s went to 0 but the pool was still saturated for 14 s, read p95 was 807 ms and checkout p95 was about 38 s. It hides the problem rather than fixing it.

A checkout-api problem outlasting the gateway (runbook step 3): the replay put the end of errors 4.4 s after gateway recovery, and in the metrics checkout 5xx stopped (last point ≥1% at 09:21:30) before gateway 5xx stopped (09:21:35). The fault depends on the gateway burst and does not continue on its own.
report.counterfactual_evidence: Deployed config (new retry policy, burst, pool 15, connection held): 124 503s, of which 105 were pool timeouts and 68 were read requests; pool saturated for 76 s; checkout p95 40,568 ms; read p95 10,000 ms. Old retry policy restored: 93 503s, all gateway pass-throughs on checkout POSTs; 0 pool timeouts; 0 s saturated; checkout p95 11,125 ms; read p95 49 ms. Gateway burst removed: 0 503s. Connection released before the gateway call: 33 503s, all gateway; 0 pool timeouts; 0 s saturated; read p95 49 ms; but checkout p95 was still 37,938 ms because of the retries. Pool raised to 30: 33 gateway 503s; 14 s saturated; read p95 807 ms. Restoring the old retry policy alone prevents the pool exhaustion.
report.documentation_evidence: Not consulted. The retry behaviour described here (retry on 503, retry POST, back-to-back attempts) comes from the diff and is confirmed by traces such as req-01832, which shows 4 POST charge attempts with no gaps between them. It does not come from library documentation.

runbook: QueuePool pool_size=5, max_overflow=10, pool_timeout=10; connection held through the gateway call
report.remaining_uncertainty: The evidence covers checkout-api-3 only; I assume the other 5 instances, which run the same deploy, behaved the same way. I did not check whether retried POST charges caused duplicate charges, because gateway-side idempotency behaviour is not in the evidence. Dashboard values I read by eye were checked against query_metrics. The replay is a simulation of the incident traffic, not a production rerun.
report.recommended_fix: 1. Now: roll back dep-8841 (kubectl rollout undo deployment/checkout-api), or restore the old Retry settings: status_forcelist={502,504}, allowed_methods={'GET'}, backoff_factor=0.5. 2. Do not retry the non-idempotent POST /v1/charges unless it has an idempotency key; if 503 retries are wanted, use backoff and set an overall deadline on the charge call. 3. Longer term: release the DB connection before the gateway call and reacquire it to commit. In the replay this removed pool exhaustion even with the new retry policy. Also consider a separate pool or bulkhead for read endpoints, a lower pool_timeout, and alerting on db_pool_in_use at capacity. Raising pool size alone is not enough.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Gateway 503 burst (trigger) + dep-8841 retry policy (retries 503 on POST, 4 attempts, no backoff) while holding DB connection through gateway call -> pool exhaustion (15/15) -> db_pool_checkout_timeout 503s on all endpoints including /cart and /orders.
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: 105 of 124 503s are 503_pool_timeout (42 /orders, 37 /checkout, 26 /cart); 19 are 503_gateway, e.g. req-01832 with 4 POST charge attempts over 31s holding a connection; diff adds 503 to status_forcelist, allowed_methods=None, backoff 0.
